6: Ad revenue attribution
7: Ads display in the app on banners, offer walls, interstitials, etc., and create ad revenue.
8: Ad revenue, combined with in-app purchases and subscription revenue, provides you with the complete LTV picture of the user. By matching user LTV to the media spend campaign, you can determine ROI and analyze it on the platform.
9: Attributed ad revenue data
10: :
11: Is acquired from the mediation platforms or ad monetization networks via server APIs or by embedded reporting SDK in the app (including iOS 14).
12: Is attributed to the media source that originally brought the user, for example:
13: User sees an ad from Network A and downloads your app.
14: Ad displays inside the app.
15: Ad revenue is attributed to Network A (responsible for user acquisition), regardless of who published the ad.
16: Reporting granularity depends on the monetization network integration and ad revenue attribution type.
17: Integration types for ad revenue attribution
18: Data accuracy and freshness depend on the ad revenue attribution integration type, as shown in the following table.
19: Note
20: : SDK integration types require developer assistance to implement. S2S integration types require you to have the correct network credentials.
21: Ad revenue attribution integration type
22: Description
23: Aggregate level
24: via S2S API
25: AppsFlyer receives daily revenue, broken down by geo.
26: The effective revenue per action (eRPA) is derived by dividing the revenue by the number of instances of a trigger event.
27: The trigger events are either app open or specific in-app events set in the app.
28: If you're using a mediation platform, make sure to disable ad revenue integrations for monetization partners mediated via the platform before enabling the ad revenue integration with the platform. Failure to do so results in duplicate data.
29: Data is not available in raw data reports and cannot be shared with ad networks via postbacks or UA signals.
30: Device-level
31: via S2S API
32: The mediation platform or monetization network reports the revenue by user at the device level. Not all networks support device-level granularity.
33: This revenue is attributed to the media source that brought the user. Meaning AppsFlyer ad revenue attribution adheres to the attribution rules found in the platform, including retargeting attribution rules.
34: If you're using a mediation platform, make sure to disable ad revenue integrations for monetization partners mediated via the platform before enabling the ad revenue integration with the platform. Failure to do so results in duplicate data.
35: Device-level via S2S API includes 100% of ad revenue and offers the highest data accuracy among ad revenue integration types.
36: Data is available in raw data reports and can be shared with ad networks only via

23: LTV vs. Activity
24: There are two methods for analyzing user event data. Event data relates to actions performed by users post-installation, such as in-app purchases, registrations, and level completions. In AppsFlyer, event data is available grouped by the user acquisition date or the event date.
25: Post-install event data grouped by user acquisition date is referred to as lifetime value (LTV).
26: Post-install event data grouped by event date is referred to as activity.
27: Note
28: : Installs are neither LTV nor activity.
29: Advertisers find both types of data useful but for different purposes. For this reason, both are available.
30: LTV data
31: LTV data are the events performed during the lifetime of a user who converted/installed the app in a specific date range. The date range refers to users who installed during the time period and shows how valuable they are during their time as customers. If a user converted/installed the app before the specified date, then even if events occurred during the specified date range, they don't show in LTV dashboards and reports.
32: LTV data is a tool that shows the
33: quality of users
34: from different media sources. Campaign optimization depends on LTV data.
35: Activity data
36: Activity data shows what users did during a specified date range. meaning what events were performed by active app users during a specified date range. It doesn't matter if the users converted/installed the app outside of the date range.
37: Because activity data shows a breakdown of chronological events, it's useful for measuring the overall performance of media sources during specific date ranges. For example, use activity data to see how many purchase events were performed by all app users during a specific month.
38: Use activity data to compare user behavior in the current month relative to a previous month.
39: The train analogy
40: This analogy will help you understand the difference between activity and LTV data.
41: Activity:
42: Imagine you're watching a passing train. As the train passes, you see only the actions performed by the passengers on the train as they pass by. This is activity data.
43: LTV
44: : Now imagine, that you board a train as an observer. The train is divided into railroad cars.
45: You board the car with other passengers at the departure platform. This is the install.
46: During the journey, you're able to observe all the actions performed by the passengers in the car. You observe the actions of these passengers until a passenger deboards the train, this is an uninstall.
47: You aren't able to view the actions of passengers in other railroad cars because they boarded the train before or after you. This then is LTV.
48: AppsFlyer dashboards and reports—LTV or activity?
49: The dashboards enable marketers to optimize their non-organic traffic. Most of the dashboards are LTV-based, as marketers typically measure performance on an LTV basis. All aggregated data reports are LTV-based, and all raw data reports are activity-based.
